key_phenomenon_and_validation: Quiescent zero-power baseline; main power contactor de-energized (0.0 V, 0.0 A, 0.0 W).
Capacitive DC bus charging inrush transient: peak power 34.6 W vs. 15.6 W IDLE baseline (2.22x spike in 200 ms).
Steady-state IDLE waiting state; constant 15.6 W power draw; zero spindle cutting load (wear rate 0.0 µm/s).
Low-speed cutting (s=1): wear rate 0.80 µm/s (30.0 -> 37.92 µm); FIR/DSP filter successfully suppresses anomalous 73.7 W electrical noise spike at t=16.6 s to 48.9 W.

High-speed cutting (s=3): wear rate accelerates 2.875x to 2.30 µm/s; cutting power drifts +10.98% (90.2 W -> 100.1 W) and chatter vibration drifts +18.75% (1.60 g -> 1.90 g) as wear increases from 38.0 µm to 83.77 µm.

Non-preemptive machining window: true wear reaches 80.09 µm at t=40.3 s; estimated wear crosses 80 µm warning threshold at t=40.9 s (80.08 µm); machining safely finishes at t=41.9 s with wear 83.77 µm (< 100 µm breakdown limit) before immediate PM transition.
Preventive maintenance window: machine transitioned to low-power STANDBY (3.6 W); spindle disengaged; physical tool insert swapped (wear reset to 0.0 µm).

Post-PM re-engagement at s=3: inrush spike of 182.1 W at t=50.1 s; sharp tool cutting power drops to 82.5 W (-17.6% power reduction vs. 100.1 W worn tool at t=41.9 s); vibration drops to 1.36 g (-28.4% reduction).
